items.title: The universal property of the localisation at a multiplicative subset
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that a ring map f from A to B sending every element of a multiplicative subset S to a unit factors uniquely through the localisation S^{-1}A (statement lines 1300-1311, with the commuting diagram drawn in the statement). The proof does not cite the universal property from elsewhere: it defines g on a fraction by f(x) f(s)^{-1}, notes that well-definedness follows from the definition of the localisation, and then proves uniqueness by computing the value of any competing map on 1/s and reducing a general fraction to a product (proof lines 1313-1325). The computation on 1/s is where the hypothesis that f inverts S is used, and the author writes both halves in full. H2.
